title: Virtual Machines

header.html: Deploy and manage Azure compute resources (20-25%)
Create a virtual machine; configure Azure Disk Encryption; move a virtual machine to another resource group, subscription or region; manage virtual machine sizes; manage virtual machine disks
the official Microsoft Learn AZ-104 study guide, skills measured as of October 26, 2023

html:
1Creating a virtual machine

An Azure virtual machine (VM) is IaaS: you manage the guest operating system, Azure manages the host hardware.

Choice at creation Notes
Subscription, resource group, name, region Region decides latency, cost and available sizes
Image Windows Server, Linux distributions, or a custom image
Size CPU, memory, storage, network capacity
Authentication Password or SSH key (Linux)
Disks OS disk, optional data disks
Networking VNet, subnet, public IP, NSG
Management Boot diagnostics, managed identity, auto-shutdown, extensions

VM extensions run post-deployment tasks (install software, run scripts, configure). Stopped (deallocated) VMs do not charge for compute, but disks still cost; a VM that is only stopped from inside the OS keeps billing for compute.

Exam tip

. To stop compute billing, stop the VM from the portal (state "Stopped (deallocated)").

2Sizes

Family For
B (burstable) Low baseline CPU, bursts: dev/test, small sites
D (general purpose) Balanced CPU and memory
E (memory optimized) Databases, in-memory
F (compute optimized) CPU-heavy workloads
N (GPU) Graphics and machine learning

Resizing changes the size: it may require a restart, and if the new size is not available on the current hardware cluster, you stop (deallocate) the VM first. [Verify live]

3Disks

Disk Fact
OS disk Holds the operating system; persistent
Data disk Additional persistent storage; attach, detach, resize
Temporary disk Local to the host, for page and swap files; data is lost on redeploy or some maintenance
Managed disks Azure manages the storage account; types: Standard HDD, Standard SSD, Premium SSD, Premium SSD v2, Ultra Disk

Increase a disk's size by deallocating the VM (for most cases), then resizing the disk; you cannot shrink a disk.

Exam tip

. Important data never goes on the temporary disk (drive D: on Windows).

4Disk encryption

Option What it does
Server-side encryption (SSE) Default for managed disks, with platform-managed keys (or customer-managed keys)
Azure Disk Encryption (ADE) BitLocker (Windows) or DM-Crypt (Linux) inside the VM; keys in Azure Key Vault; encrypts OS and data disks
Encryption at host Encrypts temporary disks and caches at the host

ADE needs Azure Key Vault in the same region and subscription with the right access policy (enabled for disk encryption).

5Moving a VM

Move How
To another resource group or subscription Move the VM and its related resources (disks, NIC, public IP) with the portal's Move action; the VM's location stays the same; the resource ID changes
To another region Use Azure Resource Mover (or Site Recovery), or re-create from a template, disk copy or image
Exam tip

. Stopped from inside the OS is not deallocated: compute billing continues until the VM is stopped in Azure.

6Exam Q&A

6.1 Practice questions (choose the best answer)

S1A team wants to stop paying for VM compute at night. What should they do?

  • AShut down only from inside the guest operating system
  • BStop the VM from the Azure portal so it is deallocated
  • CDelete the OS disk of the virtual machine each night
  • DDetach the network interface of the virtual machine
Show the answer

Answer: B. Deallocated VMs do not incur compute charges.

S2Where should a VM store application data that must survive a redeploy?

  • AA data disk
  • BThe temporary disk
  • CThe page file
  • DThe boot diagnostics container
Show the answer

Answer: A. The temporary disk can lose data; data disks persist.

S3An administrator wants BitLocker encryption for a Windows VM with keys held in Key Vault. Which feature fits?

  • AA resource lock
  • BAn availability set
  • CA budget
  • DAzure Disk Encryption
Show the answer

Answer: D. ADE uses BitLocker with keys in Key Vault.

S4A VM must change to a larger size. What is true?

  • AThe VM must be recreated from scratch with a new operating system disk
  • BDisks must be deleted and re-created before the new size can apply
  • CIt requires a new subscription that supports the larger size
  • DIt may need to be restarted, and sometimes deallocated first
Show the answer

Answer: D. Resizing can require a restart or deallocation.

S5A team moves a VM to another subscription. What else should move with it?

  • AIts disks, network interface and public IP
  • BNothing
  • CThe storage account for another app
  • DThe Entra tenant
Show the answer

Answer: A. Related resources move together with the VM.

S6Which VM size family suits memory-intensive databases?

  • AB (burstable)
  • BF (compute optimized)
  • CE (memory optimized)
  • DN (GPU)
Show the answer

Answer: C. The E family has a high memory-to-CPU ratio.

6.2 Recall questions

R1What does a deallocated VM stop charging for?

Show the answer

Compute.

R2Which disk loses data on redeploy?

Show the answer

The temporary disk.

R3What does Azure Disk Encryption use on Windows?

Show the answer

BitLocker, with keys in Azure Key Vault.

R4Can you shrink a managed disk?

Show the answer

No.

R5Name two managed disk types.

Show the answer

For example Standard SSD and Premium SSD.

R6What runs post-deployment tasks on a VM?

Show the answer

VM extensions.

7Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
Create image, size, auth, disks, networking, extensions
Billing deallocated = no compute charge; disks still billed
Disks OS, data, temporary (not persistent); managed types
Encryption SSE default; ADE (BitLocker/DM-Crypt, Key Vault); encryption at host
Move resource group or subscription with related resources; region via Resource Mover
